findings.title: Validate the effective budget snapshot rather than rereading enumerable input properties
findings.trigger: Provide a valid Partial<VmBudget> object with inherited or non-enumerable known properties, or an enumerable getter whose first value differs from later reads.
findings.cause: The result is constructed using input[key] for every known key; validation then iterates Object.keys(input) and rereads input[key]. Effective values missing from Object.keys or changed after snapshot creation escape validation.
findings.expected: Every returned budget value must satisfy safe-integer, minimum and fixed-Profile maximum checks; unsupported keys must still reject.
observed: Inherited executionMs=1001 is accepted above the fixed 1000.
Non-enumerable heapBytes=67108864 is accepted above the fixed 33554432.
An enumerable maxJobs getter returning 10001 first and 1 later is read four times; the accepted snapshot retains 10001 above the fixed 10000.
findings.effect: Host configuration can increase execution/heap/job budgets under the unchanged Profile ID/hash, violating the versioned tighten-only contract. createPluginVm consumes the returned heap budget at runtime.setMemoryLimit and uses the other effective budget fields.
findings.reachabilityLimit: This is a confirmed public configuration API defect. No guest-controlled production input path or native privilege escalation was established. Compiled WASM memory, separate admission reservations and other fixed limits remain in place; no claim of their bypass is made.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Read each supported property once, validate the effective snapshot rather than input rereads, and keep unknown-key rejection. Alternatively explicitly reject unsupported descriptors/prototypes. Add permanent regressions; review and regenerate Profile hashes after repair. Do not alter native admission records merely to make the hash check green.
